title: Block: A 2-D DP Table Over Two Strings
oneLiner: Find the length of the longest substring two strings share, with a table indexed by prefixes of each.
keyTakeaway: For two sequences, make the table (n + 1) by (m + 1) so row 0 and column 0 mean "empty prefix", and compare a[i - 1] with b[j - 1]. That offset is where the bugs live.
explanation:
Return the length of the longest contiguous run of characters that appears in both a and b. "banana" and "ananas" share "anana", length 5.

dp[i][j] is the length of the common run ending exactly at a[i - 1] and b[j - 1]. If those characters match, the run extends the one ending one character earlier in both: dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1. If they don't, no run ends here: 0. The answer is the largest entry. Longest Common Subsequence and Edit Distance use the same table and indexing with a different rule when characters differ.

    # 3. If a[i - 1] equals b[j - 1], dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1; otherwise it stays 0.

gotchas: Comparing a[i] with b[j] in a table that has the extra empty row and column, which is off by one.
Carrying the best value forward when characters differ (that is the subsequence rule, not the substring one).

complexity.note: Every pair of positions is filled once with O(1) work; the table is (n + 1) by (m + 1), or one row if you only keep the previous row.
